newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh wants more G7 access for poor nations.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh wants more G7 access for poor nations.

text.p: Bangladesh has urged Group of Seven (G7) nations to extend duty-free access to exports from Less Developed Countries to stop them from slipping further behind the industrialised world, officials said on Tuesday.
The powerful G7 had also been asked to facilitate greater flows of foreign direct investment into the LDCs, they said.

Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina made the requests in a letter to G7 heads of state or government on behalf of 48 LDCs ahead of the group's summit to be held next month in Denver, the United States.
Dhaka acted as spokesman for LDCs during the Uruguay Round of international trade negotiations. The Uruguay Round eventually led to the creation of the World Trade Organisation.
"The process of globalisation might accentuate inequality in poorer countries," Hasina was quoted by one official as saying in her letter to G7 leaders.
Copies of the letter were given to the heads of G7 missions in Dhaka on Monday, officials said.
The G7 comprises Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and United States.

Hasina said LDCs -- nations mainly in Africa but also dotted around the Asia-Pacific -- received less than 0.4 percent of foreign direct investment inflows and accounted for only 0.4 percent of international trade.
She also called for bilateral and multilateral debt relief and the reorientation of aid programmes for infrastructure development.
